To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a large subset of MOFs in the Cambridge Structural Database can be identified and characterized with respect to surface area and porosities; (ii) these MOF structures exhibit a wide range of hydrogen adsorption properties, with the most porous materials exhibiting hydrogen adsorption capacities of ∼1 wt%; (iii) the theoretical hydrogen storage capacity of these MOF structures is limited by their surface areas and the strength and extent of hydrogen binding.
1) We have identified ∼4000 MOFs with nontrivial porosity from a catalog of 20,000 CSD compounds.
